title: 债券不再是避风港：美债却逆势反弹，避险逻辑生变？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Let me turn to you, Ruth, because we saw the stock markets in the US recover after we got some relief and the treasury side of things. But that wasn't necessarily because of US economic
segments.zh: 让我转向你，Ruth，因为在美国市场方面，我们看到一些缓解后，权益资产有所回升。但这并不一定是因为美国经济基本面。

segments.en: fundamentals. Yeah, absolutely. And I think that's key. This is definitely not a move that is
segments.zh: 是的，绝对如此。我认为这是关键。这绝对不是由经济疲软或整体基本面支撑的走势。

segments.en: underpinned, you know, by a softening economy or fundamentals as a whole. This is a rush for
segments.zh: 这是对安全资产的追逐。

segments.en: safety. We saw early in the session yesterday, you know, French bonds come under pressure, guilt's under pressure with, you know, 30 years hitting the highest levels since 1998. Now,
segments.zh: 昨天早盘，我们看到法国债券承压，英国国债也承压，30年期收益率触及1998年以来最高水平。

segments.en: all this meant that bonds, as we know, are no longer a haven. But treasuries, well, perhaps treasuries that have been sold off are. And that's why we saw that bid across the curve in the US during the
segments.zh: 所有这些意味着债券不再是避风港。但美国国债，或许那些已被抛售的国债，可能是。这就是为什么我们看到美国国债收益率曲线在纽约时段出现买盘，

segments.en: New York session, led by the front end, the two-year part of the curve. Again, that's easy to digest, that's, you know, less sensitive to, you know, long-term fiscal risks and all that. So as a result,
segments.zh: 由前端、两年期部分引领。这容易理解，对长期财政风险等不太敏感。因此，

segments.en: investors did buy treasuries because they have been sold off heavily and they thought, you know what, perhaps it's just time to get a little bit of a nibble into treasuries just for that buffer.
segments.zh: 市场参与者确实买入了美国国债，因为它们已被大幅抛售，他们认为，或许现在是时候稍微配置一些美国国债，只是为了缓冲。
